scope: CPU-bound parsing optimization; direct lexer from baseline is unchanged
retainedChanges: Direct construction of successful non-root identifier, literal and constant leaves

method.outliers: Drop one minimum and maximum, average remaining 10
modes: Repeated parsing of one snapshot (cache may be warm)
Fresh snapshot per parse, lexing excluded from parse timer
method.timers: process.hrtime.bigint; natural garbage collection; sequential runs, no parallel benchmark processes
method.reproduction: npm run build; node lib\test\scripts\benchmarkLexParse.js Q:\src\DataConnectors 7 12 > results.json

attempts.name: Baseline
attempts.description: Parser implementation at 99b7fd7; updated measurement harness only.

attempts.name: Attempt 1: bounded checkpoint rollback
attempts.description: Iterate only IDs allocated after the checkpoint; preserve AST-before-context deletion order. No full-map scans or sorting.

attempts.name: Attempt 2: add indexed line bounds
attempts.description: Attempt 1 plus O(1) diagnostic line bounds using token start/end line numbers instead of a document-prefix scan.

attempts.name: Candidate separate-process repeat
attempts.description: Same candidate as attempt 2, no additional optimization.

attempts.name: Baseline separate-process repeat
attempts.description: Saved compiled 99b7fd7 library, same updated compiled harness, run after candidate to reverse initial execution order.

attempts.name: Round 2 baseline
attempts.description: Bounded rollback and indexed diagnostic lines; no child-list or leaf changes.

attempts.name: Owned mutable child lists
attempts.description: WeakMap tracks ownership of appendable child arrays, invalidated on collection copy to preserve shared-array isolation. Overhead outweighed saved copying; implementation removed.

attempts.name: Owned mutable child lists only above 32 children
attempts.description: Limit WeakMap ownership and mutable appends to wide lists. Still slower than round 2 baseline; implementation removed.

attempts.name: Direct identifier and literal leaves
attempts.description: Register successful non-root single-token identifiers and literals directly as AST nodes, without transient context objects or context-map insert/delete.

attempts.name: Extend direct leaves to constants
attempts.description: Attempt 09 plus required, optional, closing, and text-matched constants. Roots, token mismatches and constant-text mismatches retain normal contexts; token-consumption failures reconstruct the pending context before rethrowing.

attempts.name: Direct leaf separate-process repeat
attempts.description: Same production implementation as attempt 10, measured before baseline to reverse initial execution order.

attempts.name: Round 2 baseline separate-process repeat
attempts.description: Saved compiled pre-child-list implementation (attempt 06), same compiled harness, measured after candidate.

attempts.name: Round 3 baseline
attempts.description: Bounded rollback, indexed lines and direct identifier/literal/constant leaves; no type-lookahead bypass.

attempts.name: Skip impossible primary-type attempts
attempts.description: Non-mutating token/text classification in readType avoids failed primitive contexts, checkpoints and discarded diagnostics. Required types, root reads, EOF, overridden checkpoint/restore hooks and enabled tracing retain the original path.

attempts.name: Type-lookahead separate-process repeat
attempts.description: Same optimization as attempt 15, with the classifier's partial switch rewritten as conditionals to satisfy exhaustive-switch lint. Run before baseline to reverse initial execution order.

attempts.name: Round 3 baseline separate-process repeat
attempts.description: Saved compiled attempt-14 parser, same compiled harness, measured after the candidate.

profiles.method: Node inspector CPU profiler; 2 warmups then 4 reused-snapshot parses of Siteimprove; lexing and module startup excluded; self-sample percentages, not wall-time attribution

alternatingConfirmation.method: Baseline and candidate in same process; alternate execution order each round; fresh lexing outside timer
alternatingConfirmation.caveat: Both libraries loaded together. Confirms large-file gains but reports smaller-file regressions; module coexistence/JIT/GC effects were not isolated. Retained, not discarded.

validation.scope: 7 production connectors with CombinatorialParserV2; 51 resource files, 12 additional valid/invalid expressions, and all prefixes of a typed-function section with both built-in parsers.
regressionTests: checkpoint.test.ts: no full-map keys scan, no-op rollback, gaps, AST/context cleanup, nested rollback and ID reuse
lexerSnapshotCache.test.ts: indexed versus scanned bounds for mixed newline forms, multiline literals, quoted identifiers, combining characters

directLeaf.test.ts: no transient leaf contexts on success; IDs, attributes, ranges, parent/child/kind maps and rightmost leaf; root fallback; cancellation at token consumption; missing optional/required/closing constants; constant-text invariant failures.

interpretation: Aggregate benefit is dominated by Siteimprove and CCHTagetik; no universal small-file improvement is claimed.
Bounded rollback accounts for most of the improvement. The incremental wall-time gain from indexed bounds is smaller and not isolated from run-to-run variance.
CPU sampling after the changes points to context creation/finalization, node-kind maps and allocation/GC as the next investigation targets.
No synchronous-parser rewrite, AST shape change, reduced validation, or disabled node maps was introduced.

leafInvestigation.baseline: Attempt 06 already includes bounded rollback and indexed line bounds. Percentages below are incremental, not relative to 99b7fd7.
interpretation: Both leaf runs show an aggregate improvement in both snapshot modes; no universal per-file speedup is claimed.
WeakMap bookkeeping for mutable child-list ownership regressed the corpus and was removed, even though broad-list differential checks passed.

Direct leaves preserve final AST/state/error results. Successful leaves no longer have a transient context visible during tracing or cancellation callbacks; those intermediate callback observations are not claimed equivalent.
Natural GC, machine load and process allocation history still affect the modest incremental gains; these repeats are not a statistical confidence interval.

typeLookaheadInvestigation.selectionDecision: User retained the direct lexer, algorithmic efficiency and bookkeeping reductions, and removed type-lookahead speculation. Its implementation and optimization-specific test file were removed; all measurements, profiling and differential results below are historical.
typeLookaheadInvestigation.baseline: Attempt 14 includes all prior retained improvements. Percentages here are incremental, not relative to 99b7fd7.

profiles.method: Node inspector CPU profiler; 2 warmups then 4 reused-snapshot parses of Siteimprove; lexing and module startup excluded; self-sample percentages, not wall-time attribution

validation.coverage: Both built-in parsers; primitive and structured types, literal/identifier expressions, quoted/case-sensitive names, malformed inputs, root/non-root and required/fallback reads; complete context state compared with the speculative path forced through a forwarding checkpoint hook; custom hooks, enabled tracing, and pre-cancelled reads.

developmentFindings.finding: The first untimed differential check found an EOF-state mismatch. readToken leaves currentToken on the last token at EOF, but checkpoint restoration clears it. Skipping that restoration changed pending-context tokenStart.
developmentFindings.resolution: Exclude EOF from the bypass instead of changing normalization semantics. Add a focused EOF regression. Timings 15 and 16 include this correction.

interpretation: Both runs improve both aggregate parse modes, but reused-snapshot gains are modest (about 2-2.5 percent) and per-file results vary.

CapacityMetricsCES, Databricks and BQECore are slower in both modes on both runs. The repeat shows approximately 10.1/5.7/7.1 percent reused-snapshot regressions respectively. Initially retained for the aggregate workload benefit, especially fresh parses of Siteimprove and CCHTagetik, then removed by user choice.
Fresh snapshots benefit more, consistent with avoiding discarded diagnostics and their position/cache work. This is a plausible explanation, not an isolated attribution of all saved wall time.
Profiles are sampled on Siteimprove only. A zero observed diagnostic self-sample count is not proof that all diagnostic construction has been eliminated.
No primitive-type leaf expansion, synchronous-parser rewrite, binary-reduction rewrite or tracing API change is included in this attempt.
